claims.match_notes: The full identifier remains private. The late entry date is reported without assuming an Army-to-OSS sequence.

claims.claim_text: Santro Calcara has an unresolved identity conflict: official and institutional records document OSS soldier Santoro Calcara under an identifier that differs by one digit from the index.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The indexed spelling and private identifier do not exactly agree with the Santoro Calcara record repeated in official Army data and an institutional Operation Ginny roster.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Conflicting. The rare surname, close given-name spelling, OSS context, and near identifier are suggestive, but the one-digit identifier disagreement prevents a merge.
claims.temporal_assessment: The candidate's 1944 OSS mission is documented, but no identity, occupation, employer, or chronology is assigned to the indexed Santro record until Box 101 resolves the conflict.
claims.match_notes: Full identifiers and the Army candidate's entry details remain private. The Santoro spelling is not silently substituted for the printed Santro spelling.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The visually checked index prints Santro Calcara and a private identifier. person_updates.identity_evidence: The visually checked index gives Sam Caldarea and a private identifier in Box 101. No exact-name Army record was found. person_updates.next_action: No reliable pre-OSS employer has yet been identified in the accessible sources reviewed. person_updates.identity_evidence: The exact distinctive name Morris Calden appears in an authoritative National Diet Library inventory as a Foreign Economic Administration researcher on several 1944 Japanese-industry reports. The index supplies no private identifier or corroborating detail, and no source links that federal work to Box 101 or establishes its sequence relative to OSS.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 101 for birth year, residence, government transfer records, exact OSS entry date, and documents establishing whether Foreign Economic Administration work preceded, overlapped, or followed OSS service.
